open_points.subject: K-02 function filesystem boundary
open_points.text: “no filesystem beyond its input” and “declared output out”; K-06 also permits a function to produce a file
open_points.question: How does a function produce a file output if it may access no filesystem location other than its input?
options: permit a bounded output/scratch path
require file bytes to be returned through a non-filesystem interface
forbid function-produced files
open_points.default_guess: Permit a bounded, kernel-provided output path and no other writable filesystem.

open_points.subject: K-03 operation declaration
open_points.text: “An operation binding gives one manifest operation typed input and output ports”
open_points.question: What authoritative record declares the operation’s effect class, HTTP request construction, response validation and idempotency-key placement?
options: the pinned manifest operation record
the owner-accepted binding
separate kernel records
open_points.default_guess: Put all of them in the pinned manifest operation record and expose them through the accepted binding.

open_points.subject: K-03 manifest observation
open_points.text: “When that digest no longer matches, invocation is refused”
open_points.question: How and when does the kernel obtain or refresh the current manifest so it can observe a changed operation digest, and what happens if the manifest cannot be read or validated?
options: read it on every relevant request
explicit installation reload
watched cached manifest
open_points.default_guess: Read and validate the installation-selected manifest before binding acceptance and invocation, failing closed when unavailable.

open_points.subject: K-04 contract-version lifecycle
open_points.text: “A contract is an immutable versioned declaration” and “the first contract of a new slot name creates the slot”
open_points.question: What happens when a new contract version is authored for an existing slot: does it become the slot’s current contract version, and what happens to its existing activation and flows pinned to older versions?
options: new version becomes current without an activation
new version becomes current only after an implementation is admitted
versions have no slot-level current pointer
open_points.default_guess: Make the new version current only when one of its implementations is admitted and activated; already pinned flows retain the older version.

open_points.subject: K-04 run pins
open_points.text: “A run pins what it uses”
open_points.question: Exactly which mutable selections are pinned by a run—flow version, function activations, implementations, bindings, manifest operation digests, service instances and built requests—and at what point are they pinned?
options: pin everything at run creation
pin each node when it becomes runnable
use current selections at every attempt
open_points.default_guess: Pin the flow, bindings and function activations at run creation, while recording the exact built request for each operation attempt.

open_points.subject: content-addressed identities
open_points.text: “an existing one when the content is equal” and implementations are “identified by the digest of the code together with its contract version”
open_points.question: What canonical representation and digest algorithm define equality and identity for contracts, implementations, trial cases and flow versions?
options: canonical serialized content with a specified digest
raw submitted bytes
store-defined structural equality
open_points.default_guess: Use a specified canonical serialization and cryptographic digest, with implementation source normalized only by that serialization.

open_points.subject: K-05 captured failure oracle
open_points.text: “a failed real execution can be captured into it, so a repaired slot stays repaired”
open_points.question: What result must a later implementation produce for a captured failed execution when the failed execution supplied no known-correct output?
options: only complete successfully with schema-valid output
owner supplies the expected output
a case carries a separately declared predicate
open_points.default_guess: Require successful completion with contract-valid output, without asserting an exact output value.

open_points.subject: K-05 corpus changes
open_points.text: “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus” and adding a case yields “the trial case every later implementation must pass”
open_points.question: When a case is added, are existing verdicts and the current activation re-evaluated or invalidated, and how can an older implementation obtain an admitted verdict over the enlarged corpus for rollback?
options: automatically re-admit every implementation
invalidate verdicts and require explicit resubmission
keep old verdicts but test only later implementations
open_points.default_guess: Invalidate corpus-dependent verdicts, re-evaluate the active implementation immediately, and allow explicit re-admission of older implementations.

open_points.subject: K-05 deterministic admission
open_points.text: “Admission is a deterministic verdict” while trials have bounded time, memory and processes
open_points.question: What execution-environment facts are pinned so that admission is deterministic, including Python/runtime version, standard-library version, platform and resource-limit interpretation?
options: pin a versioned sandbox image and limit policy
treat the installation environment as implicit
promise only repeatability within one process
open_points.default_guess: Pin a versioned sandbox image and a versioned resource-limit policy.

open_points.subject: K-06 schema equality
open_points.text: “An edge is valid when both ports carry the same schema”
open_points.question: What does “the same schema” mean: identical schema identity, canonical structural equality, or semantic equivalence between differently written schemas?
options: identical canonical schema digest
structural equality after normalization
schema compatibility
open_points.default_guess: Require an identical digest of a canonical schema representation.

open_points.subject: K-07 guard semantics
open_points.text: “a guard on a declared closed value”
open_points.question: What is the source and type of the closed value, what comparison does a guard perform, and what observable value or status results when the guard is false?
options: enum equality and skipped downstream nodes
boolean condition and absent output
branch selection among declared alternatives
open_points.default_guess: Use equality against a declared enum value and mark the guarded node and its dependants skipped.

open_points.subject: K-07 map semantics
open_points.text: “a map of a node over a collection”
open_points.question: What ordering, result shape and failure behavior does a map have when one or more element executions fail or wait?
options: ordered results with per-element status
fail the whole map on the first failure
allow only all-success output
open_points.default_guess: Preserve input order, record every element attempt, and make the map node fail if any element fails.

open_points.subject: flow inputs and outputs
open_points.text: “A flow’s own inputs and outputs are values, never files”
open_points.question: How are flow input and output ports declared, supplied, validated and represented when a guarded, mapped or failed path produces no value?
options: required typed ports with explicit optional/union schemas
nullable values
implicit values inferred from graph edges
open_points.default_guess: Declare typed boundary ports explicitly and require absence to be represented in the schema rather than implicitly.

open_points.subject: K-08 unknown applied outcome
open_points.text: “only the owner’s resolution moves it: applied, or not applied” and “the run continues”
open_points.question: If the owner resolves an attempt as applied but the response was lost, what output is supplied to downstream nodes that consume that operation’s output?
options: effect operations with unknown outcomes may have no output
owner supplies or selects a recovered output
the node remains output-incomplete and its dependants cannot run
open_points.default_guess: Do not allow a dependent output to be fabricated; mark the effect applied but fail or skip dependants requiring the unavailable output.

open_points.subject: K-08 resend identity
open_points.text: “An effect resolved as not applied is sent again only with a fresh approval” and “The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key”
open_points.question: Does the resend use the original idempotency key or a new one, and is it a new attempt or a replay of the original attempt?
options: same key and new attempt record
new key and new attempt record
same attempt record updated
open_points.default_guess: Use the same stable operation identity/idempotency key and create a new immutable attempt record.

open_points.subject: K-08 pending classification
open_points.text: “When the kernel cannot tell whether an effect happened” and K-09 separately names “a service is unreachable”
open_points.question: Which transport outcomes are classified as definitely unsent/unreachable versus outcome unknown, especially connect failure, timeout, connection loss and malformed response?
options: phase-specific deterministic classification
treat every transport failure as unknown
treat every response-less failure as unreachable
open_points.default_guess: Classify failures before any request bytes can have reached the service as unreachable and every later ambiguous failure as outcome unknown.

open_points.subject: K-09 immutable traces and retries
open_points.text: “Every node execution writes one immutable trace record” while nodes may rest, resume and be tried again
open_points.question: Is a trace record created per node, per execution attempt or per state transition, and how are pending-to-resumed status changes represented without mutating it?
options: immutable event records plus attempt records
one mutable node trace
one final trace written only after completion
open_points.default_guess: Use immutable attempt and state-transition records, with the run’s current status derived from them.

open_points.subject: K-09 mixed-branch completion
open_points.text: “A failed node stops only its dependants”
open_points.question: When independent branches succeed, fail, wait or are skipped in the same run, when does the run end and which terminal status and outputs does it expose?
options: continue independent branches then derive a precedence-ranked terminal status
stop the entire run at the first failure
return separate branch outcomes without one run status
open_points.default_guess: Continue independent branches, then end failed if any required node failed and expose only outputs whose declared producers succeeded.

open_points.subject: K-09 cancellation and refusal
open_points.text: “a refusal ends the run `refused`” and “the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent”
open_points.question: What happens to function executions or HTTP requests already in progress when cancellation or refusal ends the run, and how are late responses recorded?
options: attempt cancellation and record late outcomes without scheduling more work
wait for in-flight work before ending
end immediately and discard late outcomes
open_points.default_guess: Stop scheduling, attempt to terminate sandbox work, retain immutable records of any already-sent operation’s eventual or unknown outcome, and never feed late outputs forward.

open_points.subject: K-11 fixed MCP surface
open_points.text: “one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner’s approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel”
open_points.question: Which MCP operations carry the primary actions omitted from that fixed list: add a trial case, capture a failure, release a failed run, roll back a slot, propose a binding, compose/prove a flow, and refuse an effect?
options: expand the fixed operation list
define explicit sub-actions under the listed generic verbs
remove the omitted primary actions
open_points.default_guess: Define explicit typed sub-actions under `author` only where genuinely authoring, and add distinct release, rollback and refuse operations.

open_points.subject: K-11 MCP transport
open_points.text: “over `mcp`” together with “one inbound channel, `mcp`, behind the host’s reverse proxy” and “No HTTP surface of the kernel’s own”
open_points.question: Which MCP transport connects the reverse proxy to the kernel listener, and does “no HTTP surface” prohibit MCP over HTTP or only non-MCP HTTP endpoints?
options: MCP Streamable HTTP is the sole HTTP endpoint
MCP over a non-HTTP local transport behind the proxy
another specified MCP transport
open_points.default_guess: Use MCP Streamable HTTP as the sole endpoint and interpret the exclusion as prohibiting non-MCP HTTP APIs.

open_points.subject: K-12 recent repair context
open_points.text: “that slot’s recent traces and trial evidence”
open_points.question: What deterministic rule defines “recent,” and may the agent page or request older relevant traces and evidence?
options: fixed count with pagination
fixed time window
all retained records
open_points.default_guess: Return a fixed newest-first page and permit pagination over all retained records.

open_points.subject: K-14 disclosure order
open_points.text: “open, business_confidential or personal_data” and “the highest class”
open_points.question: What is the exact ordering of disclosure classes, and does an input accepting a class also accept every lower class?
options: open < business_confidential < personal_data with downward acceptance
three unrelated labels
explicit accepted-class sets per input
open_points.default_guess: Order them as listed and let a maximum accepted class admit that class and all lower classes.

open_points.subject: K-14 function input policy
open_points.text: “a function’s output takes the highest class its execution received” while only bindings declare “the highest class each input accepts”
open_points.question: What disclosure ceiling applies to each function input port, and what class does a zero-input function produce?
options: contract declares input ceilings and zero-input output class
functions accept every class and zero-input outputs are open
derive ceilings and output class from trial data
open_points.default_guess: Put input ceilings and a base output class in the immutable function contract; join the base class with received inputs.

open_points.subject: K-14 caller-supplied values
open_points.text: “Every value carries” a disclosure class and “A flow’s own inputs and outputs are values”
open_points.question: Who assigns and is trusted to assign the class of a caller-supplied flow input, and can an agent label personal data as `open`?
options: flow boundary declares a fixed class
only the owner may assign a class
caller supplies a class that the kernel trusts
open_points.default_guess: Declare the class on the immutable flow input port and do not let a caller downgrade it per run.

open_points.subject: K-14 owner channel
open_points.text: “An agent never receives a `personal_data` value” and “The owner receives every value,” while the owner “reaches the kernel through the agent channel”
open_points.question: How does the kernel deliver raw personal data through the agent channel without exposing it to the language-model agent that mediates that channel?
options: a distinct owner-visible response path in the same client
end-to-end encrypted owner-only payloads
the agent channel is only transport and the agent cannot inspect owner-token responses
open_points.default_guess: Require a distinct owner-authenticated, owner-visible response path whose raw payload is not placed in the model context.

open_points.subject: K-15 token configuration failure
open_points.text: “the kernel reads the token list again whenever it has changed” and revocation “takes effect at the agent’s next request”
open_points.question: How is a change detected atomically, and does the next request fail closed or continue using the cached list when the changed token configuration is unreadable or invalid?
options: atomically replaced versioned file and fail closed
cached list remains active on reload failure
configuration service with version tokens
open_points.default_guess: Use an atomically replaced versioned configuration and fail closed after a detected but invalid change.

open_points.subject: K-15 authentication outcomes
open_points.text: “Agents act for the owner with tokens” and “The owner’s actions, each agent’s and the kernel’s own are distinguishable”
open_points.question: What observable refusal applies to a missing, invalid, ambiguous or wrong-role token, and how are owner and agent token identities guaranteed not to collide?
options: typed authentication refusal and disjoint token records
generic refusal with a reason only in the trace
proxy authenticates and supplies an actor identity
open_points.default_guess: Use disjoint owner/agent credential records and return a typed unauthenticated or unauthorized refusal without creating an action record attributed to a principal.

open_points.subject: K-17 idempotency scope
open_points.text: “Idempotency keys, exact replay and outcome handling exist only on operation nodes” versus K-08’s “The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key” in the discussion of effects
open_points.question: Do `read` and `draft-write` operation nodes also receive idempotency keys and exact-replay records, or are those guarantees limited to state-transition, external-effect and destructive attempts?
options: all operation nodes
all write classes including draft-write
only approval-stopping effect classes
open_points.default_guess: Record exact attempts for every operation node but require idempotency keys for every non-read operation.

open_points.subject: K-17 restart behavior
open_points.text: “one process with one store and one writer,” runs may rest, and there is “no durable workflow engine” or “store-continuity mechanism”
open_points.question: After the kernel process restarts, are awaiting, pending and in-progress runs recoverable and resumable, and how are operation attempts interrupted at the crash classified?
options: recover waiting runs and mark ambiguous in-flight sends outcome_unknown
all unfinished runs become failed
restart recovery is outside the product guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Recover persisted waiting runs; classify any sent-but-unresolved operation attempt as outcome_unknown and any unsent interrupted function attempt as failed.

open_points.subject: direct-service personal-data scope
open_points.text: The changed exclusion says K-14 “covers what the kernel itself returns,” while Actors says “values of class `personal_data` reach an agent only as digest and class”
open_points.question: Is the no-raw-personal-data promise limited to kernel responses, or does it also constrain an agent’s newly acknowledged direct access to microservices?
options: kernel responses only
all agent access including direct service access
direct access is allowed only for data not classed personal_data
open_points.default_guess: Limit K-14 to kernel responses and revise the broader actor statement to say so.

open_points.subject: changed exclusion cross-reference
open_points.text: “as for processing a photo (decision 17)”
open_points.question: Does “decision 17” refer to K-17, which is about process/store guarantees, or to item 17 under “Questions settled,” which describes direct photo processing?
options: Questions settled item 17
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a reference to Questions settled item 17 and name that section explicitly.
